thread:
alex: CI job gh-actions/ci-gpu-224 just turned red on main — failing test `tests/quant_attention::test_long_context` with CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS on h100-202. Not flaky, reproduces in the job logs.

jamal: can you paste the job link and the short stack snippet?

alex: https://ci.internal/runs/224 (logs attached in job). snippet:
```
E cuLaunchKernel (attention_forward_kernel): CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS
    at /workspace/ops/attention.cu:432
    at run_attention (attention.cc:210)
    at forward (model.cc:87)
```

sophie: did infra flip drivers recently? that looks like a kernel-level address error, sometimes driver mismatch or a bad kernel build. :eyes: 

alex: infra rolled nodes to driver 535.86.05 yesterday night, but some workers are still on 530.41 — CI pool might be mixed. all h100 nodes in that shard were updated though.

marco: interesting — illegal address often indicates a kernel or memory corruption. can you repro locally with the same docker image from the job? if yes we can narrow to model change vs runtime.

alex: trying now. repro command I'm using:
```bash
# pull the exact CI image used by job
docker pull registry.internal/redwood/ci-gpu:2026-03-10-535
# run the single test on GPU 0
docker run --gpus all -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 -v $PWD:/src registry.internal/redwood/ci-gpu:2026-03-10-535 \
  bash -lc "cd /src && pytest -q tests/quant_attention.py::test_long_context -k long_context -q"
```

jamal: try `export CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` too so we get synchronous stack traces, and `cuda-memcheck` if that fails. also confirm kernel names/ptx in the image: `nm /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so` may be different across driver versions.

ci-bot: rerun requested by <@alex> — queued job gh-actions/ci-gpu-224-rerun-1.

alex: rerun failed again, same error, different host h100-209. attaching cuda kernel logs (excerpt):
```
[ 7673.122345] nvidia: Xid (PCIe ERR) 47, PID 224: GPU hang: loading kernel module failed, process killed
[ 7673.122416] nvidia: EGPU: cuLaunchKernel returned 710 (ILLEGAL_ADDRESS)
```

sophie: can infra confirm whether any CUDA toolkit/driver mismatches were introduced in the image? sometimes base image has CUDA 12.3 libs but nodes are on driver X.

infra-oncall: checking node images and driver inventory now. quick note: we rolled host driver on the h100 fleet but container base images were not rebuilt — that can surface mismatches for certain PTX/SM combos. will report back within 20m.

marco: in parallel please open a short bisect: we should compare the last green commit vs current head for attention kernels — if it's a regression in our op, patch likely introduced memory indexing error on long contexts. also try the exact failing test with an a100 node to see if it's h100-specific.

alex: ack — starting bisect: range origin/main~15..main and kicking off tests on an a100 pool. I'll post results here.

jamal: thanks. if infra confirms mixed drivers, we should pin the CI pool to a single driver version and block merges until we stabilize. also pinging runtime-team to check recent attention kernel refactor.

infra-oncall: update: we found 3 nodes that still had 530.x kernels but were incorrectly marked as updated. they've been drained. scheduling an immediate CI run on a fully-homogeneous shard and will post job id.

alex: thanks — re-running locally with CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING gave a clearer stack: looks like an index calc in attention_forward for sequence lengths > 8192. that points to a model-side off-by-one. starting a small patch to guard bounds and re-running unit tests.

marco: good find. keep infra posted if the homogenous rerun still fails, otherwise we'll assume it's our bug and proceed with the patch + quick canary to main. :thumbsup: 

jamal: adding note to PR: "potential memory indexing fix for long-context attention; CI failures on h100 exposed illegal address."

alex: will open PR with fix and mark it WIP. thanks all.
